To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the French National Registies of Childhood Cancer are able to fulfil surveillance missions satisfactorarily and support the national program of research on childhood cancer.
The incidence of childhood cancer in mainland France during 2000– 2004 was 156.5 per million children per annum, with a sex-ratio of 1.1.

(i) incidence of cancer in children is close to that of other industrialized nations; (ii) incidence of cancer is higher than that reported in the 1990s; (iii) incidence of cancer varies with age; (iv) incidence is higher in males than females; (v) incidence of haematological cancers is twice that of solid tumours; and (vi) incidence of cancer has been stable over time.

the incidence of childhood cancers in France and their geographical distribution.
the development of a system for the collection and analysis of data from the French National Registies of Childhood Cancer.
the epidemiology and aetiology of childhood cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the French childhood cancer incidence rates are in the upper range of those reported in other countries, but the data are not sufficiently reliable to support the conclusion that the incidence of cancer is higher in France than in other countries.
the incidence of cancer in French children is similar to that of the most developed countries, but higher than the incidence in France in the 1990s.
the incidence of childhood cancer in the 21st century is increasing in France.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the French national registries are able to provide high quality data on incidence of childhood cancer in mainland France.

the incidence rates of childhood cancer in our country are close to those in other industrialized countries and that the French National Registories of Childhood Cancer are a reliable tool for monitoring the incidence and survival of childhood cancer.

the French National Registres of Childhood Cancer are able to fulfil their mission of public health surveillance, and to support the national programme of research on childhood cancer.
